title: Functorial stable-page representatives of the etale image filtration
statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category and D its diagram of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with cone c. Let F_i be complexes of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], uniformly zero below an integer a, with compatible inverse-image transition maps [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] satisfying the identity and composition laws [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. Let G be their pullbacks to c.pt with a colimit cocone L. Fix integers p and q. Let H identify with their degree-p cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], with transitions given by canonical derived pullback P followed by the complex transition. Use the image-filtration predicate of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-hypercohomology-filtration-zero]. There exist functorial first hypercohomology spectral sequences, ordinary-sheaf first-page identifications with the termwise transition and comparison equations, vanishing in negative resolution degree, and one uniformly stable page N in bidegree (p-q,q). For every class in filtration step q, a stable-page representative is defined naturally in transition maps; its being zero is equivalent to membership in step q+1, and a zero canonical limit image gives zero image under the stable-page comparison. No colimit-comparison assertion is included.

source.place: Lemma 59.52.1, proof; Derived Categories Tag 015J, functorial image filtration and support bounds

proof.text: Obtain uniform spectral sequences, canonical filtrations, stable-page graded isomorphisms, and restricted transition and limit maps.

Identify each image predicate with the image of its canonical filtration-step inclusion. Choose its unique representative (uniqueness follows from monicity); project to the cokernel and apply the inverse stable-page isomorphism. The restriction equations and the identifications H give transition membership and equality of representatives. Cokernel naturality proves class naturality. Exactness of the inclusion/cokernel short complex identifies a zero class with the next filtration step. A zero limit abutment image forces the restricted filtration image to be zero by monicity, hence its graded projection and stable-page image are zero.
